transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for helping out. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. 

However, you should avoid strenuous or heavy exercise, heavy lifting, and swimming for a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the info! I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them after surgery, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure whether it's okay to use in your specific case, I'd recommend checking with your care team to be certain.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, I'll make sure to check with my doctor. Another question I have is, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
No problem! It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. 

However, I don't have your specific details, so I can't say exactly where you are in your recovery. If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Going back to your light sensitivity question - if it's mild and things just seem brighter than usual, sunglasses outside should help. But if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's everything I wanted to ask. Thank you so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thanks again for answering all my questions!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery.
